archie_exclusive.label: AI-powered genealogy (OCR, face matching, 5 public record APIs)

categories.name: Orchestration Frameworks
categories.description: Libraries for building multi-agent systems. You write code, define roles, and wire agents together. Multi-agent is now table stakes -- every major framework shipped it by early 2026.
categories.archie_edge: These are libraries you build with. A.R.C.H.I.E. is a running system -- GPU-aware routing, warm-boot lifecycle, physical security, and 39 autonomous background jobs out of the box. No assembly required.
categories.archie_gap: LangGraph offers durable execution with checkpoints. Google's A2A protocol enables cross-platform agent communication -- A.R.C.H.I.E. doesn't support either yet.

categories.name: Workflow Builders
categories.description: Visual drag-and-drop platforms for connecting LLMs to tools and data sources. Strong for no-code teams. Dify leads with RAG and prompt orchestration.
categories.archie_edge: Workflow builders connect pipes. A.R.C.H.I.E. manages the entire factory -- agents, models, hardware, security, and operations.
categories.archie_gap: Dify and n8n offer visual drag-and-drop workflow builders that non-developers can use. A.R.C.H.I.E. currently requires code or CLI to configure workflows.

categories.name: Autonomous Coding Agents
categories.description: AI-powered coding tools that write, edit, and debug code. Claude Code now has Agent Teams (Opus 4.6). Devin dropped to $20/mo. Cline hit 5M+ installs. Cursor crossed $500M+ ARR.
categories.archie_edge: A.R.C.H.I.E. is a full platform, not just a coding tool -- coding is one of 46 modules. These tools write code; A.R.C.H.I.E. runs the whole operation.
categories.archie_gap: IDE integration, speed, and laser focus on developer experience. Coding agents are purpose-built for code; A.R.C.H.I.E. is purpose-built for everything.

categories.name: Enterprise Platforms
categories.description: Enterprise-grade platforms with teams, permissions, audit trails, and vendor support contracts.
categories.archie_edge: Self-hosted, no vendor lock-in, own infrastructure. Full data sovereignty with zero cloud dependency.
categories.archie_gap: Enterprise support contracts, compliance certifications from big-name auditors, and larger professional services teams.

categories.name: Self-Hosted & Open Source
categories.description: Open source alternatives focused on local-first AI. Privacy-first, community-driven, no vendor lock-in.
categories.archie_edge: Full platform vs individual tools. A.R.C.H.I.E. is unified -- agents, models, security, operations, and fleet management in one system.
categories.archie_gap: Simpler setup, lighter weight, focused scope. These tools do one thing well; A.R.C.H.I.E. does 46 things.

categories.name: Self-Improving & Accountable
categories.description: This category doesn't exist yet in the market. A.R.C.H.I.E. created it.
categories.archie_edge: A platform that measures, audits, and proves its own improvement with data. Not just AI that works, but AI that gets better and can show the receipts.

trends.name: OpenClaw
trends.description: The one that started the "claw" craze. A personal AI assistant that lives in your messaging apps (Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage). Went viral, creator joining OpenAI. Simple, elegant, one agent doing one thing well.
trends.verdict: Brilliant personal assistant. Not an operations platform. Like comparing a Swiss Army knife to a command center.

trends.name: PicoClaw
trends.description: OpenClaw's little sibling. Runs on a $10 microcontroller with just 10MB of RAM. Perfect for IoT, embedded systems, and proving AI can run anywhere. Impressive engineering, completely different mission.
trends.verdict: Cool tech, opposite universe. PicoClaw fits in your pocket. A.R.C.H.I.E. runs your entire operation.

trends.name: Claw Empire
trends.description: A pixel-art game layer on top of Claude Code and Codex CLI. You "conquer" coding tasks in a retro game interface. Fun, viral on TikTok, but it's a skin -- the actual AI is someone else's.

vs_archie.label: Full platform, Own AI, Own infrastructure

trends.verdict: Great marketing, zero original AI. When the game ends, you're still using Claude Code. A.R.C.H.I.E. IS the platform.

trends.name: NemoClaw
trends.description: Nvidia's enterprise version of OpenClaw, announced at GTC March 2026. Adds AI guardrails, governance, and safety -- features that overlap with A.R.C.H.I.E.'s IAAE ethics system. Still alpha, but Nvidia backing makes it serious.
trends.verdict: The only one worth watching. Nvidia + governance is serious. But A.R.C.H.I.E.'s IAAE is already live and production-tested -- NemoClaw is still alpha.

tool_stack_comparison.title: How Many Tools to Match A.R.C.H.I.E.?
tool_stack_comparison.tagline: One platform vs. a patchwork of nine
tool_stack_comparison.still_missing: And you'd still be missing agent welfare, warm-boot lifecycle, station-based dispatch, mission profiles, self-auditing codebase, Telegram escalation, and a unified knowledge base tying it all together.

ksm_comparison.title: Kytran Server Manager vs Vanta, Drata & More
ksm_comparison.intro: Compliance platforms charge $15,000-$100,000/year. Kytran Server Manager is free, open-source, and self-hosted.

differentiators.title: One-Click Remediation
differentiators.description: Vanta and Drata tell you what's wrong. Kytran Server Manager fixes it with a single click. The only compliance tool with built-in remediation.
differentiators.verdict: No competitor offers scan + fix in one tool.

differentiators.title: STIG Compliance Scanning
differentiators.description: 138 rules across Ubuntu, Docker, and Network STIGs with .ckl STIG Viewer export. Zero competitors offer STIG scanning.
differentiators.verdict: DoD-grade compliance in an open-source package.

differentiators.title: Self-Hosted & Open Source
differentiators.description: Your data never leaves your servers. No SaaS vendor lock-in, no annual contracts. Audit the code yourself.

differentiators.title: AI-Powered Analysis
differentiators.description: AI compliance analysis explains findings in plain English and suggests prioritized remediation plans. Premium tier feature.
differentiators.verdict: No compliance competitor has integrated AI analysis.

building_transparency.title: A2A Protocol
building_transparency.description: Google's Agent-to-Agent standard lets agents from different platforms communicate. A.R.C.H.I.E.'s agents talk internally but can't yet interop with external agent systems.

building_transparency.title: Cloud Auto-Scaling
building_transparency.description: Elastic cloud compute that scales to zero and spins up on demand. A.R.C.H.I.E. scales via fleet GPU nodes with OTA provisioning -- hardware fleet scaling, not cloud auto-scaling. Trade-off: zero cloud bills, but requires physical hardware.

building_transparency.title: Visual Workflow Builder
building_transparency.description: Drag-and-drop interface for non-developers to build AI workflows. A.R.C.H.I.E. requires code or CLI configuration. A visual builder would open the platform to broader teams.

building_transparency.title: Durable Execution
building_transparency.description: Checkpoint-based execution that survives crashes and can resume from any point. A.R.C.H.I.E.'s jobs restart from the beginning if interrupted.
